# `Q-18-3` — Engine Runtime Not Found

> An execution engine needs an external runtime (e.g. Julia, R, or
> Jupyter) that could not be found on this machine, so the render
> could not continue.

## What this means

Some engines are Quarto integrations for a language runtime that lives
outside Quarto itself — Julia, R (via knitr), or a Jupyter kernel. The
engine extension is present and resolves correctly, but when Quarto
tried to launch the runtime it needs, that runtime was not on `PATH`.

This is a missing local dependency, not a problem in your document:
the same document renders fine on a machine where the runtime is
installed.

## Why this happens

- The runtime (e.g. `julia`, `Rscript`, `jupyter`) is not installed.
- The runtime is installed but not on the `PATH` Quarto sees — for
  example an IDE or CI environment with a different `PATH` than an
  interactive shell.
- An environment variable that names a specific runtime executable
  (for example `QUARTO_JULIA`) points at a path that does not exist.

## How to fix

The message names both the engine and the runtime it could not find.

1. Install the named runtime, or make sure it is on `PATH` in the
   environment Quarto runs in.
2. If you use an override environment variable to point at a specific
   executable, confirm that path is correct.
3. Re-run the render once the runtime is available.

## Related errors

- [`Q-18-1`](Q-18-1.qmd) — the engine ran, but its result was not in
  the shape Quarto expects.
